t: If any provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional, or the applicability thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the constitutionality of the remainder of this Act and the applicability thereof to other persons and circumstances shall not be affected thereby.

fable.w: This is a standard severability clause that preserves the rest of the Act if one part is struck down. The tempting reading is that the reference to a provision being declared unconstitutional implies litigation against the government, but the clause grants no outside party a right to sue or object. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or advisory body involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: If any provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional, or the applicability thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid

qwen_block.w: This is a standard severability clause. It addresses the legal status of the statute if a court invalidates part of it. It does not establish any process for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. It merely preserves the rest of the law in the event of judicial invalidation.
qwen_block.s: If any provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional, or the applicability thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the constitutionality of the remainder of this Act and the applicability thereof to other persons and circumstances shall not be affected thereby.

opus.w: This is a boilerplate severability clause. It keeps the rest of the Act in force if part of it is invalidated, and it involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or rulemaking. Its mention of a provision being declared unconstitutional describes what follows from a court ruling. It does not give an outside party a right to sue over a federal decision, so it does not count as participation.
opus.b:
This is a standard severability clause, so it does not involve participation.

**The tempting reading:** Because it talks about a provision being "declared unconstitutional" or "held invalid," it might look like it lets outside parties sue the government. That reading fails. The clause only says what happens to the rest of the Act if a court strikes part of it down. It does not give anyone a right to sue, object to, or comment on a federal decision. No outside party is brought into any federal decision.

It does not establish any mechanism for public participation, consultation, or coordination with outside parties before a federal decision is made. The mention of 'any person' refers to the scope of the law's application, not to a participatory role.
qwen_chat.s: If any provision of this Act is declared unconstitutional, or the applicability thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the constitutionality of the remainder of this Act and the applicability thereof to other persons and circumstances shall not be affected thereby.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the statute mentions "any person," it implicitly involves the public.
